issues.title: Single-program results are labelled and summarised as if certified; the list of one-program results is incomplete
issues.location: Theorem labelled thm:sy header (main.tex:311); Results-in-brief row (main.tex:102); Method (main.tex:234-235); Status paragraph (main.tex:335-336); Prop. prop:ceiling discussion (main.tex:394-395); Corollary for 236 (main.tex:354-355); Stadlmann ceiling (main.tex:273-274)
issues.analysis: The Method section fixes the evidence standard: "A value counts as certified when both programs return the same two rationals." (main.tex:234-235). Item (2) of Theorem thm:sy, the capped numerator on which the headline 236 statement rests, does not meet it: "This item and Proposition~\ref{prop:kin-own} below are the results of this note that so far rest on one program" (main.tex:335-336). Yet (a) the theorem header carries no "one program" qualifier, whereas Prop. prop:kin-own's header does ("[\lbl{Computed}, exact rational arithmetic, one program]", main.tex:343); (b) the Results-in-brief row for the Song--Yue witness reads "& \lbl{Computed}, Thm.~\ref{thm:sy}\\" (main.tex:102) while the next row says "one program"; (c) the 236 corollary (main.tex:354-355) asserts that the criteria "hold" with no caveat; (d) the claim that only these two results rest on one program is contradicted by the text's own caveat on Prop. prop:ceiling: "\texttt{capped\_exact.py} has not yet re-evaluated the random point used for the weights" (main.tex:394-395). The Gram matrices come from capped_gram.py, which runs capped_check.py backwards, and are checked only against capped_check.py, so that ceiling also rests on one program's derivation. The Stadlmann ceiling 4.14 ("dual-weight bound", main.tex:273) gives no program count at all. A reader of the summary table and the theorem headers sees a higher evidence level for the 236 witness and the 212 ceiling than the body supports. A further point: the definition of \lbl{Computed} (main.tex:90, "exact certificate and a script that reproduces it") does not match the Method's definition of "certified" (two programs), so the label set is internally ambiguous.
issues.suggested_fix: Add "one program (for $J_T$)" to the header of Theorem thm:sy, to the Results-in-brief row for the witness and to the 236 corollary. Extend the sentence at main.tex:335-336 to list every single-program result (Theorem thm:sy(2), Prop. prop:kin-own, Prop. prop:ceiling and its weights, and the 4.14 ceiling), or mark those in the table. State once whether \lbl{Computed} requires two programs or only one.

issues.title: Ceiling restricted to one 846-dimensional space is stated as a bound on the best attainable ratio and as fixing which caps the 4.00438 belongs to
issues.location: Remark "what would change the picture" (main.tex:417-419); discussion after Prop. prop:ceiling (main.tex:387-392); abstract (main.tex:49-51)
issues.quote:
support: Proposition~\ref{prop:ceiling} shows that a modest change in the caps
moves the best attainable ratio below $4$.
issues.analysis: Proposition prop:ceiling (main.tex:375-382) proves only "$\frac{45J_{T'}(P1_{T'})}{I_{T'}(P1_{T'})}<3.99$ for every nonzero $P\in V$", for one specific 846-dimensional space $V$. It says nothing about $\sup_F$ over all admissible $F$, which is what "the best attainable ratio" means in this field (contrast the Stadlmann ceiling "$\sup_FkJ_T/I_T\le4.14$", main.tex:274, which really is over all $F$). Similarly main.tex:388-390 states "the caps of Lemma~9.1 cannot give their $4.00438$, which must belong to the caps of Table~3", while main.tex:393-394 concedes "We have not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its dimension". Matching dimension alone does not identify the space, and Charton et al.\ need not use polynomials from that space at all. The sentence that Lemma 9.1 values "appear to be left over from an earlier choice" (main.tex:391-392) is a guess about the authors' drafting history, not something read in the source. An expert in Maynard--Tao optimisation would object to "best attainable", since raising the degree routinely raises the ratio by amounts comparable to 0.004--0.014.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace "moves the best attainable ratio below $4$" with "moves the best ratio attainable in $V$ below $4$ (we have no ceiling over all $F$)". Replace "which must belong to the caps of Table~3" with "which is therefore consistent only with the caps of Table~3, if their function lies in $V$". Either state, from Cha26 \S11, that their $\mathcal B_{21}$ is spanned by $(L-P_1)^aP_\lambda$ with even parts and $a+|\lambda|\le21$, as $V$ is, or keep the caveat. Drop or attribute "left over from an earlier choice".

issues.title: Kintali's analytic input is described as new equidistribution estimates; the Lemma 5 remark is tied only to 240
issues.quote: step and is unaffected; the \emph{bound} $240$ depends on this input.
issues.analysis: The abstract says every preprint "combines new equidistribution estimates" (main.tex:29), and the introduction says they "pay for this with new equidistribution estimates" (main.tex:70-71). The project's own reading of Kintali (notes/sources-236.md on origin/main, \S2(d)) records that Kintali proves no new estimate. Kintali imports Stadlmann's Prop.~3 Type I/IIa/IIb/III branches, with "five source-level corrections", and picks parameters that empty Type IIc. If that reading is right, Kintali's $H_1\le236$ rests on Stadlmann's analytic input, possibly including the Type I estimate whose proof step Remark rem:lemma5 discusses. The remark then attaches the consequence only to 240 ("the \emph{bound} $240$ depends on this input"), and the 236 corollary says only "their equidistribution input". This rests on project notes, not a fresh literature check, hence the moderate confidence. Still, the manuscript's blanket characterisation is at odds with the project's documented source reading, and a reader cannot tell which of the four claims the flagged step could affect.
issues.suggested_fix: Run a bounded literature check of Kintali \S2. Then describe each preprint's analytic input accurately (e.g. "Kintali imports Stadlmann's Prop.~3 with corrections; Song--Yue prove a new estimate, Thm.~4.18"). In Remark rem:lemma5, say which claims use the Type I range of Stadlmann's Lemma 5 (240 and possibly Kintali's 236), or say that this was not determined.

issues.title: Corollary asserts that Song--Yue's criterion holds for the independent test function, which was not computed
issues.location: Corollary after Prop. prop:kin-own (main.tex:353-358); criterion stated at main.tex:298-299
issues.quote:
The variational criteria of \cite{Kin26} and \cite{SY26} hold at $k=48$, for
the published witness and for an independent test function.
issues.analysis: The manuscript defines Song--Yue's criterion as "$48J/I_0>2001/2000$" with cap-free denominator (main.tex:298). For the independent function, Prop. prop:kin-own gives only the capped ratio "$48J_T(P1_T)/I_T(P1_T)=4.0060814208\ldots>4$" (main.tex:346); $48J_T/I_0$ is not reported for it. $48J_T/I_T>4$ does not imply $48J_T/I_0>4\cdot2001/2000$ without a bound on $I_T/I_0$. The conclusion is very likely true numerically (margin about $0.004$ against a cap cost of $0.00033$), but it is not delivered. A second issue is that the note never says whether Song--Yue's analytic theorem needs the slack $2001/2000$ or only $>1$. If it needs the slack, "their criterion" is the stronger one.
issues.suggested_fix: Either report $48J_T/I_0$ for the independent $P$ and compare it with $2001/2000$, or reword as "the capped criterion $kJ_T/I_T>4$ (Kintali's criterion, and the condition Song--Yue's criterion is designed to imply) holds for an independent test function". Add one sentence on the role of $2001/2000$ in \cite{SY26}.

issues.title: "to every printed digit" cannot be checked from the note, and the quoted Kintali values are not in his normalisation
issues.quote: in \cite{Kin26}, $4.0030988$ and $4.0036348$, to every printed digit.
issues.analysis: Per the project's source notes, Kintali prints his values in Stadlmann's threshold-1 scaling to about 33 significant digits (e.g. $48J/I=1.000774701187468444763475111497864\ldots$). The note attributes to him the Polymath-scale numbers $4.0030988$ and $4.0036348$, which are rescaled truncations, and prints its own values to only 10 decimals (Theorem thm:sy(3)). A reader therefore cannot check the "every printed digit" agreement from the note, and the attributed numbers are not what Kintali printed.
issues.suggested_fix: Quote Kintali's printed values in his own scaling (with the location, e.g. Prop.~5 and p.~6), state the number of digits compared, and give the note's values to that precision, or to the agreed digits, in Theorem thm:sy(3).

issues.title: Silent switch from the declared Polymath scaling to Song--Yue's quarter scaling (threshold 1, $t$-normalised functionals)
issues.location: Results-in-brief header and row (main.tex:95, 102); \S2 convention (main.tex:122, 133-136); Theorem thm:sy items (1)-(2) (main.tex:314-317); abstract (main.tex:40-42)
issues.quote: Ratios in the Polymath scaling, where the threshold is $4$:
issues.analysis: The table announced as Polymath-scale (main.tex:95) contains the row "$48J/I_0=1.00066492>2001/2000$" (main.tex:102), which is in Stadlmann/Song--Yue scaling, where the threshold is 1. \S2 declares "We use the Polymath scaling $u=4t$" and defines $I_T,J_T$ on $T\subset L\R_k$ with $L=1.042$ (main.tex:122-136). Theorem thm:sy, however, uses $I_0$ and $J_T$ normalised in Song--Yue's $t$-coordinates. That is the only reading under which "$(98!)^2\,10^{192}\,5^{150}\,521^{50}\,I_0=I_{\mathrm{ref}}$" holds, since $10^{192}=(10^4)^{48}$ converts $x=10^4t$. Under the \S2 definitions, $I_0$ and $J_T$ differ by factors $4^{48}$ and $4^{49}$, so the exact integer identities are false as literally read. The abstract likewise reports (i) and (iii) against 4 and (ii) against $2001/2000$ with no word on the scale. The switch is signalled only afterwards, by "which is $4.0026596864\ldots$ in the Polymath scaling" (main.tex:319).
issues.suggested_fix: Before Theorem thm:sy, state that in this subsection $t=u/4$, that $I_0,J_T$ denote the functionals in $t$-coordinates (so $kJ/I$ there equals one quarter of the Polymath ratio and the threshold is $1$), and give the conversion $I^{(u)}=4^{k}I^{(t)}$, $J^{(u)}=4^{k+1}J^{(t)}$. In the Results-in-brief table give the witness row as $4.0026597$ (equivalently $1.00066492>2001/2000$ in Song--Yue scaling), and add one clause to the abstract.

issues.title: $s$, $U$, $t$, $I$ and the cap-free functionals each carry two live meanings
issues.analysis: (a) $s$: in \S2, $s(u)$ is the sum of the large coordinates (main.tex:127). In the witness, "$P(z)=\sum c\,\left(\tfrac{26}{25}-s(z)\right)^a m_\alpha(z)$" and "mass on $\{s<U\}$" (main.tex:291, 296-297) use $s$ for the sum of all coordinates. Read with \S2's definition, the witness polynomial and $I_0$ are different objects. (b) $U$: in Prop. prop:fibre, $U=U(u')$ is the fibre endpoint ("$U=\min\bigl(R,\ \max(g,\ C_{m(u')+1}-s(u'))\bigr)$", main.tex:185). In \S4, $U=\tfrac{521}{2000}$ is Song--Yue's support length, i.e. $L/4$ (main.tex:292). (c) $t$: in \S2, $t$ is the unscaled variable ($u=4t$) and the last fibre coordinate ($\{t\ge0:(u',t)\in T\}$). (d) $I$: the index set $I(u)$ and the functional $I(F)$. (e) The cap-free functionals are $I,J$ in Prop. prop:fibre ("where $I,J$ are the cap-free functionals"), but $I_0,J_0$ in Theorem thm:sy(3). The capped numerator is $J$ in the abstract and at main.tex:298 ("$48J/I_0>2001/2000$") but $J_T$ in Theorem thm:sy. In addition, $g$ is called "a threshold" (main.tex:126) while "threshold" also means the ratio bound $4$.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the large-set sum $s_g(u)$ or $\sigma(u)$. Write Song--Yue's length as $U_{\mathrm{SY}}$ (or replace it with $L/4$) and $P_U$ as $P_{\mathrm{SY}}$. Write the total sum as $|z|_1$, as Prop. prop:fibre already does with $|u'|$. Use $I_0,J_0$ for the cap-free functionals throughout, including Prop. prop:fibre, and $J_T$ in the abstract. Rename the large set $\mathcal I(u)$, and call $g$ the "largeness cut-off".

issues.title: The test-function spaces (and "degree") on which Prop. prop:ceiling is a statement are never defined
issues.location: Prop. prop:ceiling (main.tex:376-377); Prop. prop:212 (main.tex:363-365); Theorem thm:240 (main.tex:260-261); Prop. prop:kin-own (main.tex:344-345); Method (main.tex:218-219)
issues.quote:
Let $T'$ be the support with the caps of Lemma~9.1 of \cite{Cha26} and $V$ the
$846$-dimensional space above.
issues.analysis: "The space above" refers to Prop. prop:212, which mentions only "$P$ our cap-free optimiser of degree $21$ ($846$ coefficients, the dimension of the space $\mathcal B_{21}$ of \cite[Thm.~11.1]{Cha26})". The only description of the basis is the parenthetical "we use products of $(L-P_1)^a$ and even power sums" (main.tex:219). "Degree" is never defined: is it $a+|\lambda|\le D$ with $P_j$ of weight $j$? With that reading, the counts 707 ($D=20$), 846 ($D=21$) and 1041 ($D=22$) all check, which suggests the intended convention, but the reader must reconstruct it. Since Prop. prop:ceiling is a universally quantified statement over $V$, its content is not determined by the text.
issues.suggested_fix: In \S3, define $V_D=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{(L-P_1)^aP_\lambda: \lambda\text{ a partition into even parts},\ a+|\lambda|\le D\}$ with $P_\lambda=\prod P_{\lambda_j}$, note $\dim V_{20},V_{21},V_{22}=707,846,1041$ (for $k\ge D$), and state Prop. prop:ceiling for $V=V_{21}$ at $L=53/50$.

issues.title: Cap sequences incompletely specified: no $C_0$, range of $m$ in the fibre hypothesis, and Stadlmann's caps given only as "$\dots$"
issues.location: Parameter table (main.tex:143); definition of $T$ (main.tex:129); Prop. prop:fibre hypothesis (main.tex:182); main.tex:153-155
issues.quote: If $C_{m+1}\le C_m+g$ for all $m$, then the fibre $\{t\ge0:(u',t)\in T\}$ is
issues.analysis: $T=\{u:\ s(u)\le C_{m(u)}\}$ needs $C_0$ for points with no large coordinate, but caps are listed only from $C_1$ ("caps $C_1\le C_2\le\dots$"). Under the natural convention $C_0=0$ (adopted by Kintali and Charton et al.), the hypothesis "for all $m$" at $m=0$ would read $C_1\le g$, which fails for every cap set here (e.g. $0.6>0.112$). So the hypothesis is intended for $m\ge1$, and the $m=0$ case of the proof needs that admissibility is automatic. The Stadlmann row lists "$0.6,\,0.6,\,0.68,\,0.68,\dots$" without saying $C_m=0.68$ for all $m\ge3$; Lemma 9.1's analogous row is made explicit in the text (main.tex:153). The deduction "every point of $T$ has all coordinates at most $0.6$" (main.tex:272) depends on the unstated continuation.
issues.suggested_fix: Set $C_0=0$ explicitly, state the hypothesis for $m\ge1$ and add "(for $m=0$ every $u'$ is admissible)", and write the Stadlmann caps as $C_1=C_2=0.6$, $C_m=0.68$ ($m\ge3$).

issues.title: No dictionary from the sources' parameters and threshold to $(L,\tau,g,C_m)$ and threshold 4; the one-band $J_T$ is labelled Literature
issues.quote:
and the variational criterion is $kJ_T(F)/I_T(F)>4$. In this scaling the
parameters are as follows (\lbl{Literature}).
issues.analysis: The table (main.tex:141-147) gives $(L,\tau)=(1.042,0.982)$, $g=0.112$ and so on as \lbl{Literature}. The sources state $\varepsilon,A_1,\delta,B_{1,m}$ and a threshold $1$, so an expert checking the transcription must reconstruct $L=4(A_1+\varepsilon)$, $\tau=4(A_1-\varepsilon)$, $g=4\delta$, $C_m=4B_{1,m}$ and the threshold change $1\to4$. Only $C_m=4B_{1,m}$ is stated, and only for Cha26. The formula for $J_T$ with base $\tau\R_{k-1}$ and no cap on the base is the one-band ($n=1$, $A_0=-\varepsilon$) specialisation of Stadlmann's Def.~5. It is derived, not read in the source, yet it is cited as "Definitions~1 and~5 and Proposition~1". The same gap later produces the $U=521/2000$ versus $L=1.042$ confusion in \S4. That the criterion checked is the right one is the whole "why it suffices" of the note, so this dictionary is a prerequisite.
issues.suggested_fix: After the definition of $T$, add one displayed dictionary: "In the notation of \cite[Def.~1, \S6.2]{Sta26}, $L=4(A_1+\varepsilon)$, $\tau=4(A_1-\varepsilon)$, $g=4\delta$, $C_m=4B_{1,m}$, $C_0=0$; with one band ($n=1$, $c_1=c_2=0$) Stadlmann's criterion (2.1) $kJ/I>1$ becomes $kJ_T/I_T>4$ (\lbl{Proved here}, change of variables)". Include the source values ($\varepsilon=0.0075$, $A_1=0.253$, $\delta=0.028$, $B=0.15,0.15,0.17$; and Song--Yue's $U,L,\delta,B$).

issues.title: Core reduction of the corrections, the second evaluator's method and the "dual-weight" ceiling are compressed to one line each, with no pointer to the companion
issues.location: \S2 after Prop. prop:fibre (main.tex:207-213); Method item 2 (main.tex:225-228); Stadlmann ceiling (main.tex:272-275)
issues.quote: polynomials over polygons in two radial variables; so every term is an exact
issues.analysis: The step that makes capped_exact.py work is that each correction region, after symmetrisation and inclusion--exclusion, reduces to "integrals of polynomials over polygons in two radial variables". This is nonstandard. The text never says what the two variables are (the sums over the large and the small group?) or how power sums of the small group, with coordinates at most $g$ shifted by the $j$ forced coordinates, become polynomials in them. The independent program is described only as summing "directly over the exact large set, with exponential-moment generating functions", which is too little for a reader to judge the claimed independence. The ceiling "$\sup_FkJ_T/I_T\le4.14$" comes from an unexplained "dual-weight bound", and it is the only result in the note over all $F$. The companion paper \cite{Kim26} is first mentioned only in the last section (main.tex:436-438), and not at any of these points.
issues.suggested_fix: After main.tex:210, add two or three sentences naming the radial variables and the density used (or cite the exact proposition of \cite{Kim26}). In Method item 2, add one sentence on how capped_check.py integrates over a fixed large set. For the 4.14 ceiling, state the inequality used (e.g. the weighted Cauchy--Schwarz bound and its weight) or cite the companion section explicitly.

issues.title: "Cap-free part" agreement contradicts the description of capped_check.py; the provenance of $I_T$ and $J_0$ in Theorem thm:sy(3) is unstated
issues.location: Method item 2 (main.tex:227-228); Status of item (2) (main.tex:336-337); Theorem thm:sy(3) (main.tex:318-320)
issues.quote: with it on the cap-free part and is computing the $126$ correction pieces
issues.analysis: Method says capped_check.py "sums directly over the exact large set ... and has no cap-free term" (main.tex:226-228). The status paragraph says capped_exact.py "agrees with it on the cap-free part", which presupposes that capped_check.py produced a cap-free value. Theorem thm:sy(3) also reports $48J_T/I_T$ and $48J_0/I_0$, which need $I_T$ and $J_0$. Items (1)-(2) cover only $I_0$ and $J_T$, and no program is named for the other two. These are the values compared with Kintali.
issues.suggested_fix: State which program computed $I_T$, $J_0$ and the cap-free comparison (e.g. "capped_check.py run with all caps removed", or "Lemma~\ref{lem:egf} in capped_exact.py"), and how many programs agree on each of the four numbers in Theorem thm:sy(3).

issues.title: Title and summary phrasing treat the claimed bounds as bounds; "all four bounds"
issues.location: Title (main.tex:20); "What this note does not do" (main.tex:112); Corollary for 240 (main.tex:277-282)
issues.quote: \cite{Kin26}, \cite{SY26} or \cite{Cha26}; all four bounds remain conditional
issues.analysis: The title speaks of "the 2026 bounds $H_1\le240$ and $H_1\le236$", while the body correctly treats them as claimed and conditional. There are three bound values from four preprints, so "all four bounds" counts 236 twice. The 240 corollary does not cross-reference Remark rem:lemma5 even though the remark says the bound depends on the flagged step. The abstract states conditionality clearly, so this is a framing nicety, not an overclaim of substance.
issues.suggested_fix: Use "the claimed 2026 bounds" in the title; write "all four claims" or "the three claimed bounds"; add "(see also Remark~\ref{rem:lemma5})" to the 240 corollary.
